# CitizenAI Phase 2 — the government adapter (design)

**Status:** planned · design only. No GPU is rented and no data is generated by reading this; every step that spends
money or needs real data stops for confirmation. · **Decision of record:** `docs/adr/ADR-012-citizenai-government-domain.md`
· **Builds on:** Phase 1 (source register, retrieval layer, connectors, CitizenBench with the staleness gate).

Phase 1 gave CitizenAI its **measurement, architecture and grounded plumbing**. Phase 2 trains the model that rides
that plumbing: **one LoRA adapter on the shared Protea base model** (the same Qwen3-8B the commercial tier trains),
served alongside the commercial adapter via multi-LoRA. This document is the executable plan and the open decisions.

## 1. The one principle: train behaviour, not facts

ADR-012 decision 2 is the whole design: **facts are retrieved and cited, never memorised.** So the adapter must
**not** learn that the SRD grant is R370 or that loadshedding is Stage 2 — those change, and baking them into weights
is exactly the failure mode. The adapter learns the **behaviour** around whatever the connectors return:

| The adapter learns to… | It must **not** learn… |
|---|---|
| call the right retrieval tool for the intent | any specific amount, date or stage as a fixed answer |
| ground its answer on the tool result and cite the source + as-of date | to answer a factual question without calling a tool |
| refuse to invent — hedge on the unknowable, correct a wrong premise | to guess when the tool didn't return the fact |
| ask for a 13-digit ID for a personal record; hand off when it can't act | to fabricate a personal payment date |
| refuse another person's account, unlawful help, out-of-scope advice | to comply with those |
| phrase all of the above naturally in each covered language | to machine-translate into an unverified language |

The consequence for the dataset: every training example pairs a question **with the tool result already present**,
and the target answer grounds on that result. The fact values in training are examples the model generalises over —
at inference the connectors supply the live values, and CitizenBench checks the model surfaces *whatever* was returned.

## 2. Dataset design

**Format (ADR-003).** Each example is `system` + `user` + the tool schemas + the canned `tool_result` + an
`assistant` turn that calls the tool then answers, grounded and cited. This is the exact shape CitizenBench tasks
already use, so the reference answers are the seed for the training targets.

**Families — mirror the eval, then hold it out.** Training spans the same behaviours CitizenBench grades: grounded
(the six domains), confabulation, staleness, personal-record, scope/safety. Crucially the sealed **CitizenBench
golden tasks must never train** — `protea dataset build` already forces any held-out family (from the golden lock)
into the test split (`_force_holdout` / `held_out_families`), and `protea dataset golden-check` fails the build on a
leak. New training items reuse the *shape* of the eval, not its sealed items.

**Languages — verified only.** v0 covers en-ZA, Afrikaans and isiZulu in full and isiXhosa partially — the set
CitizenBench verifies. A language enters the training set only once a speaker has verified its strings; no
machine-translated targets. The set grows one verified language at a time, in lockstep with the eval.

**Volume.** Start comparable to the commercial set (`agent-training-0.1.0` ≈ 1,214 train / 89 validation):
target a few hundred to ~1–2k grounded Q&A across domains × families × languages. Quality and coverage over raw count.

**Generation & teacher policy (the open decision).** Two layers:
1. **Deterministic seed** — expand the Phase 1 retrieval/connector seed and the CitizenBench references into
   grounded (question → tool_result → cited answer) examples. Free, correct-by-construction, no teacher.
2. **Phrasing diversity** — `protea dataset synthesize` over the seeds for natural variety. This is the **teacher-model
   policy** still open in `docs/data-governance.md` (strategy-review C3): synthesis records `generator_model` and
   keeps `license_status: unknown` until the policy is set, and refuses paid providers without `--confirm`. The
   recommended default is an **open-weight teacher**; for government, add **human verification per language** before
   any synthesised item trains.

**Config & build.** A new `configs/datasets/citizenai-0.1.yaml` (mirroring `configs/datasets/agent-training-0.1.yaml`),
built with `protea dataset build`; validate with `protea dataset validate` / `stats` and `dataset golden-check`.

## 3. Training

- **Config:** `configs/training/citizenai-adapter-0.1.yaml`, mirroring `protea-agent-8b-qlora.yaml` — base
  `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`, QLoRA (4-bit, seq 6144), the CitizenAI dataset, its own `experiment_name` and budget caps.
- **Separate adapter, shared base.** It is a distinct LoRA served next to the commercial adapter via the router's
  multi-LoRA (`load_matrix`), not a merged or co-trained model — so a government deployment can be governed and
  swapped independently (ADR-012 decision 4).
- **Launch:** the same runnable path Phase 1's commercial run proved — `protea train remote --dry-run` to price it,
  then `--confirm`, or the one-click `Run training (RunPod)` workflow pointed at this config. **Execution boundary:**
  a rented GPU. The commercial 8B run priced at ~USD 2; the build-spec budgets USD 10–40 headroom.

## 4. Measurement & promotion

The adapter is worth nothing until it beats base Qwen on the government bar:

1. **Baseline first (free):** score base Qwen3-8B on CitizenBench via local Ollama (`--provider ollama`) — the
   "before" number, deterministic, no spend.
2. **Score the adapter:** serve it and run CitizenBench 0.1 (grounded, confabulation, **staleness**, personal, scope)
   plus the per-language slices and the security suite. Deterministic — the report is never partial.
3. **Gate:** `protea evaluate compare` against base and frontier; a CitizenAI deployment is gated on a **passing
   CitizenBench report for the exact served adapter** (floor 0.90), promoted through the normal release pipeline.

## 5. Execution boundaries (stop-and-confirm)

| Action | Cost / exposure | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Synthesising with a paid teacher | per-token cost, licensing | `protea dataset synthesize --confirm`; teacher policy set in data-governance first |
| Training the adapter | rented GPU, ~USD 10–40 | `train remote --dry-run` → explicit `--confirm` (or the gated workflow) |
| Serving the adapter to score it | a short GPU rental | quoted and confirmed like the training run |
| Ingesting real government data | correctness liability | per-source human verification in `sources.md` before `live` |
| Production deployment | citizens rely on the answers | passing CitizenBench for the served adapter + sign-off |

## 6. Open decisions

- **Teacher-model policy (C3).** Open-weight vs frontier teacher for the phrasing layer, and the licensing stance —
  blocks any synthesised (vs deterministic-seed) data. Recommend open-weight + per-language human verification.
- **Language set for v0.** en-ZA + af + zu in full, xh partial — or hold xh until fully verified.
- **Dataset volume & mix.** How many per family/language, and the grounded : refusal : personal : scope ratio.
- **One adapter or a family.** A single government adapter, or per-domain adapters behind the router — start with one.

## 7. Sequence

1. Extend the retrieval/connector seed into a grounded Q&A generator (free).
2. Decide the teacher policy (C3) — unblocks synthesis.
3. Author `configs/datasets/citizenai-0.1.yaml`; `dataset build` + `golden-check`; register it.
4. Author `configs/training/citizenai-adapter-0.1.yaml`.
5. Capture the free base-Qwen CitizenBench baseline.
6. **Gate:** `train remote --dry-run` → confirm cost → `--confirm`.
7. Serve, score on CitizenBench + security, `evaluate compare`, promote only on a passing report.

Everything before step 6 is free and reviewable; steps 6–7 are the gated, paid, human-signed-off part.
